source_admission: Published values and equations the study uses, with how far each was read on 2026-10-17. No outside dataset or full paper is committed; the study's other inputs are the project's committed products and the lake model's own columns. 'read' means the pages holding the values were read; 'abstract' means the abstract or a summary of it; 'secondary' means a later paper or summary quoting it; 'known' means a standard fit used from memory and checked by the tests against independent values.

sources.citation: Durisch-Kaiser E, Schmid M, Peeters F, Kipfer R, Dinkel C, Diem T, Schubert CJ, Wehrli B 2011, What prevents outgassing of methane to the atmosphere in Lake Tanganyika?, Journal of Geophysical Research 116, G02022
sources.use: Tanganyika: 32,900 km2, deepest 1,310-1,450 m, oxygen gone near 200 m, 23 Tg of CH4 in its anoxic water, 170-220 uM at 1,200 m, 6-8 uM phosphate in the deep water, a sediment release of 0.5 mol CH4 m-2 a-1, aerobic oxidation 0.02 per uM O2 a year, anaerobic oxidation with sulphate

sources.citation: Langenegger T, Vachon D, Donis D, McGinnis DF 2019, What the bubble knows: lake methane dynamics revealed by sediment gas bubble composition, Limnology and Oceanography 64, 1526-1544
sources.use: The steady porewater model of Bazhin (2003, 2010): exponential production (a 129-502 mmol m-3 d-1, b 10-43 per m, mean 30), porosity 0.9, tortuosity 1 - ln(phi^2), the critical pressure rho g h + P_atm - P_H2O with N2 at 0.78 P_atm; Lake Soppen's ebullition share of 0.05-0.3 at 9-25 m and bubbles 75-90% methane

sources.citation: Bazhin NM 2003 and 2010, theory of methane bubble formation in sediments, as Langenegger et al. (2019) set it out
sources.use: The ebullition layer and its single-gas steady solution used here

sources.citation: Crowe SA et al. 2011, The methane cycle in ferruginous Lake Matano, Geobiology 9, 61-78
sources.use: In a ferruginous, sulphate-poor lake over half of the organic matter is degraded through methanogenesis; CH4 to 1.4 mmol/L in its anoxic deep water

sources.citation: Pasche N, Schmid M, Vazquez F, Schubert CJ, Wuest A, Kessler JD, Pack MA, Reeburgh WS, Burgmann H 2011, Methane sources and sinks in Lake Kivu, Journal of Geophysical Research 116, G03006

sources.citation: Barenbold F et al. 2020, No increasing risk of a limnic eruption at Lake Kivu: intercomparison study reveals gas concentrations close to steady state, PLoS ONE 15(8), e0237836; Schmid M et al. 2005, Weak mixing in Lake Kivu, Geochemistry Geophysics Geosystems 6
